newsitem.title: FRANCE: 900 police to guard Franco-British summit.
newsitem.headline: 900 police to guard Franco-British summit.

text.p: About 900 French police will guard a two-day Franco-British summit in Bordeaux starting on Thursday, a month after a bomb attack by Corsican guerrillas on the mayor's office, officials said on Wednesday.

President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who is also mayor of the southwestern city, will host the talks with British Prime Minister John Major likely to focus on the crisis in Zaire, naval cooperation and European integration.
"Several companies of riot police and mobile units will travel to Bordeaux," said Bernard Fragneau, the official in charge of Bordeaux security.

The British and French leaders will end the summit on Friday with a lunch and news conference at city hall, repaired after a bomb blast in October by Corsican separatists seeking more autonomy from Paris.
